fieldflow.name: Service Report Digitization
fieldflow.tagline: Turn field reports into usable records, without hours of retyping.
fieldflow.title: Service Report Digitization
fieldflow.intro: A technician photographs a completed service form and sends it over chat. Back at the office, someone has to read it, re-enter the details and forward it. Here is how that work could be simplified.

spec.audienceValue: Field service businesses, maintenance teams, operations managers and coordinators

challenge.heading: Service reports get lost in messages
challenge.body: After every visit, a photo of a paper report arrives. Someone has to match it to the right job, read the details and enter them into a consistent format. As the workload grows, keeping track becomes harder.

solution.heading: Upload the report. Review the details. Move on.
solution.body: A technician would upload the report from their phone. Data could be extracted directly from digital documents or with OCR for scans and photos. AI could help with ambiguous cases where simpler methods fall short. A coordinator would review and approve the result before anything is sent.

steps.title: Upload
steps.body: The technician uploads one or more photos of the completed service report.

steps.title: Extract data
steps.body: The system extracts job details, dates and work notes. OCR can read scans; AI may assist with more complex cases.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: A coordinator checks the extracted information against the original and corrects any mistakes.

steps.title: Prepare and send
steps.body: Once approved, the system prepares a consistent PDF or structured export for an authorized recipient.

value.heading: Less data entry. Better visibility across jobs.
items: Less manual retyping and forwarding.
Consistent records that are easier to find.
Clear responsibility for review and approval.
Better visibility into missing or incomplete reports.
value.disclaimer: These are potential benefits, not measured results from a client deployment.

principles.heading: Automation with a human in control
items: Easy uploads directly from the field.
Explicit approval before sharing information externally.
Missing or uncertain data clearly flagged for review.
Traceability from the original photo to the final report.
Appropriate data protection and access controls.

invoiceflow.name: Invoice Processing Automation
invoiceflow.tagline: One place for invoices, from receipt to approval.
invoiceflow.title: Invoice Processing Automation
invoiceflow.intro: Invoices arrive by email, as attachments and on paper. Someone has to register each one, check the details and chase approvals. This example shows how a more consistent process could reduce repetitive work.

spec.audienceValue: Finance teams, accountants, SMEs and multi-site businesses

challenge.heading: Where is that invoice now?
challenge.body: Invoices sit across personal inboxes, shared mailboxes and paper folders. Details get copied manually and approvals happen in email threads. It becomes difficult to see what is pending, approved or potentially duplicated.

solution.heading: Keep invoices and approvals in one place
solution.body: Invoices would arrive in a shared queue. Data could be read from electronic invoices and PDFs, or extracted from scans using OCR. Rule-based checks would flag missing fields and possible duplicates. AI would be optional for cases that cannot be handled reliably with simpler methods. A person would review and approve each invoice before export.

steps.title: Collect
steps.body: Forward invoices to a dedicated address or upload them to a shared workspace.

steps.title: Extract data
steps.body: Read supplier, invoice number, amount and due date from structured files, PDFs or scans using OCR where needed.

steps.title: Validate
steps.body: Apply checks for missing fields, mismatches and possible duplicates.

steps.title: Assign
steps.body: Route each invoice to the right approver based on agreed rules.

steps.title: Approve
steps.body: The approver compares the original invoice with the extracted data and approves or returns it.

steps.title: Export
steps.body: Prepare approved invoices for import into accounting software.

value.heading: Less admin. Clearer invoice status.
items: One place to collect incoming invoices.
Less copying between documents and spreadsheets.
A clear record of who reviewed and approved each invoice.
Better visibility into pending approvals and due dates.
Earlier detection of possible duplicates and missing details.
value.disclaimer: These are potential benefits, not measured results from a client deployment.

principles.heading: Finance stays in control
items: Human approval before export to accounting.
Original documents available alongside extracted data.
Rule-based checks and clearly flagged exceptions.
Structured export first; direct integrations could follow later.
Role-based access and appropriate data protection.

quoteflow.name: Quote Management & Approvals
quoteflow.tagline: Build consistent quotes without copying endless spreadsheets.
quoteflow.title: Quote Management & Approvals
quoteflow.intro: When every new quote starts as a copy of an old spreadsheet, prices, discounts and document versions are easy to get wrong. Here is how sales teams could prepare and approve quotes in one place.

spec.audienceValue: Manufacturers, installers, B2B sales teams and technical service providers

challenge.heading: Every quote starts with another spreadsheet
challenge.body: Salespeople copy items from old quotes, look up current prices and adjust formulas by hand. Exceptions are approved by email, and it is not always clear which version is current.

solution.heading: Templates, pricing rules and approvals in one workflow
solution.body: A salesperson would choose a template and items from a shared catalog. Agreed pricing rules would be applied consistently, while exceptional discounts would go to a manager for approval. Each quote would have a clear version history.

steps.title: Choose
steps.body: Select a customer and quote template.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: Add items from the shared catalog and set quantities or options.

steps.title: Price
steps.body: Apply agreed pricing and margin rules automatically.

steps.title: Approve exceptions
steps.body: Send discounts or special terms outside the rules to a manager.

steps.title: Generate PDF
steps.body: Create a professional, versioned quote PDF.

steps.title: Track
steps.body: See whether each quote is in progress, sent, revised or accepted.

value.heading: Faster quoting, fewer pricing errors
items: Prepare standard quotes faster.
Reduce copy-and-paste and formula mistakes.
Use consistent pricing and approval rules.
Keep a clear history of changes and versions.
See which quotes are open or awaiting action.
value.disclaimer: These are potential benefits, not measured results from a client deployment.

principles.heading: Consistency without unnecessary rigidity
items: Templates and a shared product catalog.
Pricing rules agreed with management, not hidden in formulas.
Manager approval for exceptions before sending.
Version history for every quote.
Integrations with existing systems considered in a later phase.

shiftflow.name: Time Tracking & Timesheets
shiftflow.tagline: No more chasing work hours at month-end.
shiftflow.title: Time Tracking & Timesheets
shiftflow.intro: Employees report hours through text messages or chat, and supervisors later copy them into spreadsheets. This example shows how teams could record hours as they go and prepare payroll inputs with less chasing.

spec.audienceValue: Construction, logistics, manufacturing and field teams

challenge.heading: Timesheets become a problem just before payroll
challenge.body: Hours arrive through chat, on paper or verbally. At month-end, managers have to pull everything together, verify entries and chase missing information.

solution.heading: Record hours on mobile. Approve them as you go.
solution.body: Employees would enter hours from their phones and assign them to a job or site. Supervisors could review entries throughout the month, then export approved hours for payroll.

steps.title: Record
steps.body: Employees log their hours from a phone after each shift.

steps.title: Assign
steps.body: Link each entry to a job, site or shift.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: A supervisor reviews and approves entries.

steps.title: Resolve exceptions
steps.body: Flag missing or unusual entries for clarification.

steps.title: Export
steps.body: Prepare approved hours as payroll input.

value.heading: Less month-end admin
items: Fewer missing or unclear time entries.
Less manual consolidation at month-end.
A clear record of who approved each entry.
value.disclaimer: These are potential benefits, not measured results from a client deployment.

principles.heading: Easy for staff, clear for managers
items: Fast mobile entry that fits the workday.
Supervisor review before payroll processing.
Payroll-ready exports, with integrations considered later.
Appropriate access controls and data protection.

stockflow.name: Inventory Management
stockflow.tagline: Know what is in stock without reconciling spreadsheets.
stockflow.title: Inventory Management
stockflow.intro: When goods received and dispatched are recorded in different files, it is hard to know what is actually available. Here is how warehouse teams could record stock movements from a phone.

spec.audienceValue: Warehouses, distributors, small retailers and e-commerce businesses

challenge.heading: Different spreadsheets show different stock levels
challenge.body: Receipts, dispatches and transfers are recorded in separate places, often after the fact. It becomes difficult to establish current stock levels or understand discrepancies.

solution.heading: Record every stock movement in one place
solution.body: A team member would scan an item with a phone and record a receipt, dispatch or transfer. The shared stock view would update, with alerts when quantities fall below agreed thresholds.

steps.title: Scan
steps.body: Scan an item or QR code using a phone.

steps.title: Record
steps.body: Enter a receipt, transfer, dispatch or adjustment.

steps.title: Check
steps.body: Validate the quantity and location before saving.

steps.title: Update
steps.body: Refresh the shared inventory view.

steps.title: Alert
steps.body: Notify the team when stock falls below a configured threshold.

value.heading: A clearer picture of available stock
items: Up-to-date stock levels without reconciling multiple files.
Traceable adjustments with author and timestamp.
Less manual copying between spreadsheets.
value.disclaimer: These are potential benefits, not measured results from a client deployment.

principles.heading: Keep it practical
items: Quick mobile updates at the point of work.
Validate entries early rather than reconciling later.
A clear audit trail for adjustments.
Consider integrations with existing systems in a later phase.

fixflow.name: Maintenance Request Management
fixflow.tagline: Every reported issue has an owner and a clear status.
fixflow.title: Maintenance Request Management
fixflow.intro: A broken air conditioner, faulty lighting or an issue at a site. Requests arrive by phone and email, but it is not always clear who is dealing with them. Here is how they could be managed in one place.

spec.audienceValue: Property managers, facilities teams and multi-site businesses

challenge.heading: Maintenance requests disappear between calls and emails
challenge.body: Tenants and employees report problems through different channels. Coordinators then have to find out who took ownership, what has been done and whether the repair is complete.

solution.heading: From first report to completed repair
solution.body: Someone would submit an issue through a simple form, with an optional photo. The request would receive a priority and an owner. Coordinators could track progress and confirm completion before closing it.

steps.title: Report
steps.body: Describe the issue and attach a photo if useful.

steps.title: Prioritize
steps.body: Assign a category and priority.

steps.title: Assign
steps.body: Give the request to a technician or external contractor.

steps.title: Track
steps.body: Record updates against the request.

steps.title: Close
steps.body: A coordinator verifies completion and closes the request.

value.heading: Clear ownership, fewer forgotten requests
items: A named owner for every request.
A searchable history of issues and repairs.
Fewer requests slipping through the cracks.
value.disclaimer: These are potential benefits, not measured results from a client deployment.

principles.heading: Easy to report, easy to manage
items: Quick reporting with optional photos.
One clearly assigned owner at a time.
Coordinator verification before closure.
Appropriate access controls and data protection.

sales-assistant.name: AI Sales Inquiry Assistant
sales-assistant.tagline: Turn incoming inquiries into clear next steps, without the CRM busywork.

challenge.heading: Where the friction comes from
challenge.body: Leads arrive through email and web forms. Sales teams spend time understanding each request, finding context and copying details into the CRM.

solution.heading: How we would approach it
solution.body: An assistant could summarize the request, identify missing details and draft a response. After a salesperson reviews it, approved information could be saved to the CRM.

steps.title: Capture
steps.body: Record a new inquiry from email or a web form.

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: AI summarizes the request, identifies intent and suggests follow-up questions.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: A salesperson checks the draft and any commercial details.

steps.title: Update CRM
steps.body: Approved fields are saved through an API using defined rules.

steps.title: Respond
steps.body: External messages are sent only after approval.

value.heading: What it could improve
items: Less time spent sorting incoming leads.
More consistent CRM records.
Faster response preparation with human oversight.
value.disclaimer: Potential benefits only; no measured client results.

principles.heading: Design safeguards
items: No autonomous pricing or contractual commitments.
Human approval before external communication.
Role-based access to customer data and CRM.

nextSteps.heading: How we would validate it

steps.title: Authorize

steps.title: Retrieve

steps.title: Answer
steps.body: AI provides a concise response with document references.

steps.title: Improve
steps.body: Users flag incorrect answers for review.

value.heading: What it could improve

Easier onboarding for new team members.
Better use of existing documentation.
value.disclaimer: Potential benefits only; no measured client results.

principles.heading: Design safeguards
items: Document-level permission enforcement.
Citations and access to original sources.
No fabricated answers when evidence is missing.

nextSteps.heading: How we would validate it

workflow-coordinator.name: AI Workflow Coordinator
workflow-coordinator.tagline: Fewer missed handoffs. Clearer next steps.
workflow-coordinator.title: AI workflow coordination
workflow-coordinator.intro: Tasks move between email, chat and internal tools. Missing information and unclear ownership often become visible only when deadlines slip. This is a proposed approach, not a launched product.

spec.audienceValue: Operations teams, field service companies and project coordinators

challenge.heading: Where the friction comes from
challenge.body: Tasks move between email, chat and internal tools. Missing information and unclear ownership often become visible only when deadlines slip.

solution.heading: How we would approach it
solution.body: Rules-based automation could track task status while AI summarizes conversations and suggests next steps. Reminders and approved status updates would be handled by standard integrations.

steps.title: Detect
steps.body: Receive an event from a supported system.

steps.title: Check
steps.body: Validate deadlines, ownership and required information using defined rules.

steps.title: Summarize
steps.body: AI prepares context and suggests a next step.

steps.title: Approve
steps.body: A person approves changes with business or operational impact.

steps.title: Act
steps.body: An integration sends a reminder or updates permitted fields.

value.heading: What it could improve
items: Earlier visibility into missing information.
Less manual status chasing.
Clearer ownership and next actions.
value.disclaimer: Potential benefits only; no measured client results.

principles.heading: Design safeguards
items: Deterministic rules for deadlines and validation.
AI suggestions do not authorize critical changes.
Audit trail for every executed action.

nextSteps.heading: How we would validate it
nextSteps.body: We would test alert accuracy, usefulness of suggestions and safe action execution in representative workflows. This is not a completed implementation or client reference.

closing.body: Let's review your workflow and identify a practical first step. We will only use AI where it adds clear value.
